A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MED framework and research study. All 17 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v2, including their appendices, support reliable comparison of text, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original link-prediction, SKG application, BERT/GLUE and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds SimplE evaluations, IterDE comparisons and a sub-model-count sensitivity study.

M1.justification: Parameter sharing, neighboring-model mutual learning, evolutionary weighting, dynamic loss weighting and the BERT adaptation remain unchanged. Applying MED to SimplE adds an evaluated backbone without changing the framework.

E1.justification: Both versions use WN18RR, FB15K237, CoDEx-L, YAGO3-10, the same SKG applications and the same GLUE tasks. The added backbone and sub-model configurations do not expand dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds IterDE to the WN18RR/FB15K237 comparisons in Table 3 and Appendix A, and to the training-time comparison. The existing KGE, parameter-efficiency, SKG and BERT comparator sets are otherwise retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds SimplE as an evaluated model configuration and tests n=64, 16 and 4 for RotatE on WN18RR in Table 8. Existing dataset splits, training budgets and SKG/BERT settings are retained.

E4.justification: New Figure 4 examines training trajectories, and Section 5.6.2 tests the accuracy and training-time effects of sub-model count. ARR analysis also gains SimplE results. The component ablations are unchanged, and the existing t-SNE analysis moves to Appendix E.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v2 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 substantially expands results with SimplE and IterDE entries, training trajectories, SKG runtimes and sub-model-count comparisons. Matched main Table 3 scores remain unchanged. In Appendix A, MED's 40d TransE Hit@1 on WN18RR changes from 0.048 in v1 Table 8 to 0.038 in v2 Table 10, although v2's ablation Table 13 retains 0.048.

T1.justification: Table 1 adds SimplE's mathematical scoring definition for the newly evaluated backbone. MED's loss equations and appendix derivations remain unchanged. The newly stated standard KGE objective is explanatory; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central claims remain one-time training of croppable embeddings, effective sub-models, training efficiency and extension beyond KGE. Updating the abstract from three to four KGE models reflects additional supporting experiments rather than a new contribution claim.

C2.justification: New Section 7 qualifies empirical generality by acknowledging that the evaluated backbones are representative and that stronger KGE methods exist. Existing mechanism explanations and the relocated t-SNE interpretation are retained.

D1.justification: Section 5.1.2 newly describes candidate generation and head/tail-rank aggregation, without establishing that existing experiments changed. Table 5 adds SKG training times. Existing hyperparameters, hardware and implementation disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds IterDE, PMD, IncDE and SKDE, positioning IterDE alongside DualDE as particularly relevant. Two introductory references are removed. The overall positioning around KGE compression and knowledge distillation remains stable.

P1.justification: Most main-text paragraphs are rewritten and condensed. v2 adds Limitations and Acknowledgements sections, moves visual analysis into Appendix E, and revises author information and citation style.

P2.justification: The paper is extensively reformatted from one column to two columns. Tables are resized and restructured, appendix metrics are regrouped, and figures are relocated or expanded. v2 adds a training-trajectory figure and sub-model-count table, while enlarging the relocated t-SNE display.

improvement.justification: SimplE and IterDE comparisons strengthen validation, while the new sub-model-count study better informs accuracy and training-cost choices. These limited gains outweigh a small reporting regression: v2's changed 40d TransE Hit@1 disagrees with its retained ablation value. The core method and principal findings remain stable.
